08 — Example

Full, annotated implementation. Read it after kata submit 08 passes.

The compilable files are reference/ch08/agent/. This is the first chapter that edits the loop, and the reasoning for that is below.

The shape

steering.go   StdinSteering: a goroutine, a lock, a drain
loop.go       a steering hook, the new done condition, the partial on error
provider      the parser returns the partial message with its error
main.go       run() returns an exit code; abort prints and exits 130

Step 1 — the parser keeps what it read

if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil {
	return Message{Role: RoleAssistant, Content: content.String()}, usage,
		fmt.Errorf("read stream: %w", err)
}

Before this chapter the same line returned Message{}. That single change is what makes an interruption recoverable: the caller now has both the text and the reason it stopped.

Note that the error still wraps the original. errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) has to keep working, because that is how main decides between 130 and 1.

Step 2 — the loop keeps it too

if err != nil {
	if msg.Content != "" {
		history = append(history, msg)
	}
	reason := "error"
	if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
		reason = "aborted"
	}
	emit(Event{Type: EventAgentEnd, Turns: turn, Reason: reason})
	return Result{Message: msg, History: history, Usage: total, Turns: turn}, err
}

Three things happen before the return, and each is graded:

  • the partial message enters history, so the session can record it;
  • agent_end is still emitted, so a consumer's stream terminates properly;
  • the reason distinguishes a cancellation from a real error.

A consumer that only sees agent_end without a reason cannot tell "the user stopped it" from "the network died", and those want different messages on screen.

Step 3 — steering is drained after the turn, not before

steered := false
if opts.Steering != nil {
	for _, m := range opts.Steering() {
		emit(Event{Type: EventSteer, Turn: turn, Text: m.Content})
		history = append(history, m)
		steered = true
	}
}

emit(Event{Type: EventTurnEnd, Turn: turn})

if !askedForTools && !steered {
	emit(Event{Type: EventAgentEnd, Turns: turn, Reason: "done"})
	return ...
}

The placement is the design. Drain before the reply and the message is part of the prompt being answered. Drain after the tools and before the next request, and it arrives exactly where a person would have spoken.

steered exists because of one case: the model finished, and the person then said something. Without the flag the loop returns a final answer and silently discards the message.

Step 4 — Drain takes, clears, and returns immediately

func (s *StdinSteering) Drain() []Message {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	if len(s.queue) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	out := s.queue
	s.queue = nil
	return out
}

out := s.queue; s.queue = nil is the one-liner that prevents replay. Assigning out := s.queue[:] and leaving the queue intact looks identical in a single-turn test and repeats the instruction forever in a real run.

The reading goroutine:

go func() {
	for s.scanner.Scan() {
		line := strings.TrimSpace(s.scanner.Text())
		if line == "" {
			continue
		}
		s.mu.Lock()
		s.queue = append(s.queue, Message{Role: RoleUser, Content: line})
		s.mu.Unlock()
	}
}()

Empty lines are skipped rather than queued, because a queued empty message makes the model answer nothing and wastes a turn.

Step 5 — run returns an exit code

func main() {
	code, err := run()
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "agent: %v\n", err)
		if code == 0 {
			code = 1
		}
	}
	os.Exit(code)
}

os.Exit inside run would skip the deferred rec.Close() and could drop the last session write. Returning a code keeps the cleanup in run, where the defers live.

if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
	if res.Message.Content != "" {
		fmt.Println(res.Message.Content)
	}
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "agent: aborted")
	return 130, nil
}

130 is 128 + SIGINT. It is conventional, and it means a shell script can tell an interrupted run from a failed one without parsing stderr.

Note that persistence happens before this branch. The order is: run, persist, report. Reversed, an interrupted run loses its turn.

Why the loop is edited here

Chapter 07 could wrap the provider, because a budget only rewrites a request on its way out. Steering does something a wrapper cannot: it changes the history the loop owns, and it changes when the loop stops.

  decorator (ch07):  request in, request out
  loop hook (ch08):  history in, history plus a message out

The rule is "touch the loop only for loop state". This is loop state, and it is the only chapter where the rule is exercised.

The diffs

1. Returning an empty message on stream failure — abort-keeps-partial

- return Message{}, Usage{}, fmt.Errorf("read stream: %w", err)
+ return Message{Role: RoleAssistant, Content: content.String()}, usage, ...

2. Merging steering into the prompt — steer-enters-after-turn

- prompt = prompt + "\n" + strings.Join(lines, "\n")
+ history = append(history, Message{Role: RoleUser, Content: line})

3. Draining without clearing — steer-not-duplicated

- out := s.queue
+ out := s.queue; s.queue = nil

4. Stopping on the model's word alone — steer-continues-after-done

- if len(msg.ToolCalls) == 0 { return }
+ if len(msg.ToolCalls) == 0 && !steered { return }

Comparison checklist

  • [ ] parser returns the partial message with the stream error
  • [ ] error still wraps the original, so errors.Is works
  • [ ] loop appends the partial when non-empty
  • [ ] agent_end emitted on abort with reason aborted
  • [ ] steering drained after tools, before the next request
  • [ ] drain clears the queue under a lock and never blocks
  • [ ] empty lines skipped
  • [ ] done condition is no tool calls && nothing steered
  • [ ] session persisted before the abort return
  • [ ] exit 130 for SIGINT, 1 for errors

Differences outside this list are style.
